Amazing sequel from Metro 2033 and Last Light without a doubt. The story gets really deep and combat is great. And for a 2019 title, which is considered a revolutionary title, the game tends to go on sale on occasion I feel, which is really generous and not something you see often.

If you have played Metro 2033 and/or Last Light, I think the answer is clear: get this on sale.

[h1]A Great, Yet Flawed Finale To The Trilogy[/h1]

[h2]The Story[/h2]
I actually did quite enjoy the story here and found it was by far the most engaged I have been with the narrative of a Metro game yet, BUT:

— The plot draws from a reworked version of Metro 2035, particularly in the second half, but the delivery can feel surprisingly dull at times. Dialogue often overlaps, and there’s an overload of exposition from characters that makes it hard to stay fully engaged. That said, I liked the wide range of side characters. None of them are especially standout individually, but together they create a believable sense of camaraderie within the crew. The pacing is solid, and I appreciated how each area introduces its own faction of enemies. This avoids the common open-world problem where main antagonists disappear until the finale, instead giving each region its own smaller-scale conflicts tied to its characters.
— Adding on to the previous point, not only is a huge portion of the dialogue unbearably hand-holdy, constantly spelling things out like a tutorial, but the game also repeatedly forces you to just stand there doing nothing for minutes on end while clunky exposition is dumped on you. To make matters worse, a lot of these conversations overlap, with multiple characters talking at the same time. It might be aiming for realism compared to the usual “one person speaks at a time” approach, but in practice it’s just messy, distracting, and unnecessarily difficult to follow.
— My one major fault with the narrative is a continuation of the same one I have had throughout my entire run with this franchise, why the hell is Artyom a silent protagonist? In 2033 and Last Light it can be forgiven as for the most part in those games Artyom is flying solo, only briefly interacting with any characters which is normally nothing more than them giving orders. Exodus however is explicitly more character focused and it baffles me that they once again bound themselves by making Artyo…

The game features vivid character development and rich storytelling, paired with an excellent weapon modification system. The exploration experience is truly immersive. Before I knew it, I had already completed this unforgettable adventure!
Great graphics, gameplay, and original story. Can't ask for much more from a game.

One of the best game I've had the chance of playing. There's nothing like it. It's beautiful, the characters are charming and the art direction is phenomenal (stressing the art direction part). And when the gameplay is firing on all cylinders, its an amazing shooter even.

That being said, I think this game is starting to show its age and the lack of attention it should've received throughout the years. Bugs aren`t uncommon but they never were game breaking. Checkpoints are inconsistent and sometimes even frustrating. The broken Gamma slider, HDR, blurriness, texture streaming and performance drops (i.e.: the Taiga level) are pertinent to mention.

The karma system is infuriating and my main gripe with this game (actually all of the metro series). Its tedious. I understand its purpose but I cannot agree with its poor execution. The most egregious example might be one of the numerous stealth sections with enemies you CAN'T kill, notably in the Taiga level and in the Volga. Some sections that could've been interesting become save scumming fests, taking you completely out of the immersion - which is this game's main thing. This becomes even more of an issue with the aforementioned broken checkpoints.

I don't know where to include this in the review but I would've loved seeing a leaning mechanic. Glad to see it make its debut in Metro 2039.

Metro Exodus is one of the most atmospheric shooters ever made.
Few games manage to create the same feeling of isolation, tension, and immersion while exploring a destroyed world. The combination of survival mechanics, scarce resources, brutal firefights, and incredible environmental design makes the journey across post-apocalyptic Russia unforgettable.

What makes the game special is how immersive everything feels. You manually wipe your gas mask, charge your flashlight, clean your weapons, and scavenge every bullet like your life depends on it - because sometimes it actually does. The game constantly makes you feel vulnerable, especially during nighttime exploration or while traveling through dark underground sections.

The shift from the claustrophobic metro tunnels to larger open areas works surprisingly well and gives the world much more variety while still keeping the signature Metro atmosphere intact. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

The good:
- Incredible atmosphere and immersion
- One of the best post-apocalyptic worlds in gaming
- Excellent environmental storytelling
- Resource management adds real tension
- Beautiful visuals and lighting
- Weapon customization feels great
- Strong survival-horror elements
- Exploration is genuinely rewarding
- Sound design is phenomenal
- The train crew and character interactions make the journey memorable

The bad:
- Animations and movement can feel clunky
- Some voice acting and dialogue feel awkward
- AI can behave strangely at times
- Open-world sections occasionally lose pacing
- Bugs and technical issues still happen
- Stealth mechanics can feel inconsistent
- Certain areas drag on longer than needed
- Moral system can feel restrictive if you want the best ending
- Loading times can be annoying on older hardware

Overall, Metro Exodus is one of those rare games where the atmosphere alone carries huge parts of the experience. It’s rough around the edges sometimes, but the immersion, world design, and constant t…

The atmospheric immersion in this game completely enveloped me. The developers made the genius design choice to tie UI elements to physical items in Artyom's hands. Checking your position requires looking down at a hand-drawn clipboard map, and if a mutant tears open your gas mask, you have to physically tape over the hole. Managing your inventory via the portable backpack—while enemies are still actively roaming around you in real-time—creates a brilliant sense of vulnerability.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that certain settings or running DirectX 12 can cause the game to crash, while switching to DirectX 11 helps resolve stability issues.

citations.review_text:
As the third instalment in the franchise, Metro Exodus diverges significantly from its predecessors. While the game still features its usual weapons, characters, settings and enemies, it takes an open world design approach. Levels now feature a mini hub world where Artyom can discover enemy bases with upgrades inside, complete fetch quests/ side quests and complete main missions. The shop system has been removed in favour for a crafting system, this has lead to new mechanics but the biggest downside is that ammo and medkits are less findable in open world and have to craft them with the new 2 materials. Materials can also be used to clean weapons and repair armour and gas masks. Cleaning the weapon prevents the guns from jamming, an annoying feature that could have been left out. With these new changes and new enemies the game tends to feel like a linear Fallout game in terms of gameplay. This does not mean that the game is bad cause of these changes but it feels like an identity shift of the franchise.

However the game has technical problems such as RTX and DX12 having a high chance of crashing the game, and spatial sound Dolby Atmos setting can have certain sounds crackle. If you avoid these settings, performance (FPS) should be great.

It only gets a recommendation because when it's good, it's really good. Sadly, it's also surrounded by a bevy of technical issues that still aren't fixed to this day. Two of the major levels seem to be crash prone with no fix other than turning down the settings or forcing the game to use DX11, this is ontop of really glitchy mechanics when it comes to travel in both running, rowing, driving and ziplining. I also ran into multiple glaring animation issues where characters would just t-pose as well as the Enhanced Edition being downright broken for me and unfixable, I assume the Enchanments were more bugs. It also suffers from all the best and worst aspects of past Metro Games and the last level suffers the most from this to the point where if the ending cutscene hadn't won me back this review would've been a negative one.

Play the first two Metro games first, force DX11 and don't put the settings above high because despite having quite a hefty machine that can run bigger and more graphically intense games than this, it just crashed to desktop without warning on the later open world levels.

A masterpice of a game!

+ Beautiful graphics!
+ Good story
+ Runs great with DirectX 11

- Doesn't run good on DirectX 12(Crashing)

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as shifting from linear corridors to semi-open-world sandbox regions like the Volga, Caspian, and Taiga.

citations.review_text:
(Played on the Enhanced Edition, which doesn't have a separate Steam page for some reason)

Coming off the back of Last Light, I went into this one expecting more of the same tunnels and cramped corridors, and instead got something completely different in the best way. This time Artyom and the crew leave Moscow behind entirely and cross the country aboard a train called the Aurora, which doubles as your home base between chapters, and the game opens up into semi open locations for the first time in the series. You get a snowy stretch along the Volga, a sun scorched Caspian Sea, and the Taiga, which turned into one of my favorite levels in any game from this series, rewarding quiet, careful play and picking off patrols with a crossbow instead of guns blazing. It has this atmosphere that's hard to put into words, calm and dangerous at the same time. The open world mechanics can get a little annoying at points, mainly when you're stuck figuring out where to go next, but it's manageable and never actually ruins the experience.

What really stuck with me is that the story and the characters here are just as strong as they were in Last Light, maybe even more so, just in a different way. Your crew starts feeling less like companions who follow you around and more like an actual family you've grown attached to, and the downtime scenes on the train, where everyone just talks and interacts with each other, are some of the best moments in the whole game. It genuinely feels like real people reacting to a broken world instead of scripted NPCs waiting for their next line, and the good ending hit just as hard as I hoped it would, earned rather than handed to you. The story DLCs add a nice bit of lore on top of this too. Two Colonels stood out to me, set a year before the main story in the Novosibirsk metro with that same tense, closed in feeling the first two games had, while Sam's Story runs longer and takes things in a different direction, and even if it doesn't quite match that…

Having played and thoroughly enjoyed every single game in the Metro franchise, I can safely say that Metro Exodus is an absolute triumph. This series has consistently been one of the strongest story-driven FPS sagas in gaming history, and Exodus takes everything that made Last Light and 2033 special while taking a massive, ambitious leap forward. I genuinely have zero major complaints, and I cannot recommend this game enough.

The storytelling and atmosphere are breathtakingly good. Leaving the dark, suffocating tunnels of the Moscow metro to board the Aurora and journey across a ruined Russia is an incredible experience. Each region feels unique, tense, and alive. The narrative hits all the right emotional notes, the companions feel like real human beings you actually care about, and the sense of survival is unmatched. The gunplay is punchy, weapon customization on the fly is brilliant, and the visual direction is simply gorgeous. It grabs you from the very first minute and never lets go.

Of course, if you look at broader community feedback, a few minor nitpicks occasionally come up. Some players feel that Artyom remaining a silent protagonist during gameplay feels a bit outdated, especially when companions are having emotional conversations directly with him. A few people also miss the purely linear, claustrophobic tunnel design of the first two games, feeling that the semi-open-world areas slightly dilute the pacing. Lastly, the physical movement and controls can feel a bit heavy or sluggish for players used to fast-paced arcade shooters.

However, those small points are completely overshadowed by what the game achieves. The massive praise from both critics and fans centers on its unmatched atmospheric immersion, its phenomenal audio design, and the genuine heart of its story. It manages to expand the world without losing the dark, gritty DNA of the Metro universe.

If you love single-player shooters, rich stories, and games made with real passion, Metro Exodus …

citations.review_text: Loved it, and all the Metro Games, this one particularly, BUT only because I used a Mod that could fast forward the cut scenes, otherwise I might not have replayed it, they are long and boring (after the 3rd time)

I'm almost done with this game and in one word it's boring. The missions are sometimes entertaining, but the gameplay is clunky. The real issue is that there's way too much dialogue where your character just has to sit there and listen. No way to skip it. And the dialogue is slow. You can "explore" your environment or you can sit there and let someone talk at you while you choose to a) smoke a cigarette, b) drink your tea, or c) leave the room to go to another room where the characters talk at you some more. I know, I know. It's supposed to help you get immersed. But you're just passively sitting there. You don't even contribute. That's not very immersive/interactive. Also, there are also some places where you're just traveling and not doing much. Driving a beat up car. Or on a train. But no one is shooting at you. You don't have to defend yourself. You just drive. I got this on a discount and I won't be buying the others unless they're even cheaper than the $4 I paid for it. It sucks, because I want to like it. I know people put hard work into this. But my goodness, at least let the player skip the inane dialogue and get to the mission.
Like gameplay, weapons. A bit annoying videos that you can't skip.

citations.review_text: i want to give this game a good review but the amount of game breaking bugs that either hard crash your pc or force you to restart the chapter is absurd, i do not understand how the devs have not  fixed game breaking bugs after 7 years

Horrible glitchy bug-ridden mess. Imagine finishing wit moral points intact only for the ending to disregard it entirely. You get stiuck in the silliest places in the environnment. And the save system is a colossal ♥♥♥♥-up. Save points happen in places that make zero sense. Instead of a save point happening before a fight, it happens at the beginning of a region. Quicksave and quick load does not work on mMac, even when I changed the keybindings.

To free a prisoner in the Taiga level, you have to eliminate all nearby bandits. No problem right? two of them are so far away I thought the game was glitching out and had to restart the level-only for it to happen again. I had to google a walkthrough.

I am so disgusted with the experience of playing all three Metro games, that as much as i love the story, the bugs are unforgivable. It does not matter how good the game is if it becomes frustrating to play.

Metro Exodus, oh how much have I played you in the past, and now I finally got to finish you after so long. 

It is truly, one of the perfect games to cap off Artyom's story before the upcoming Metro 4 which reportedly will have a new protagonist. The game runs well, but there are still some bugs that apparently from what I've searched were never fixed. But nothing like a good ol' restart of the game to fix it.

The gameplay is nice, the fact that in the main story and partly (in the DLCs will not say which is which for spoiler reasons) that a bullet you fire can have dire consequences in the outcome of Artyom and his fellow Spartans' story. I do heavily recommend playing the first and second game before going into Exodus to get the context of alot of it or just watch a short story summary if so. 

Heavily recommend to get this game on sale due to it's age, but regardless it will net you a solid 15-20 hours worth of story gameplay with some replayability to get another outcome if you wish to do so. Or do some achievement hunting. 

Overall, this is a great game to play to hype yourself for the upcoming 4th game of the franchise. 

8/10. 

Now onto the next one.

citations.review_text: I didn't expect to enjoy this game as much as I did. I'm not one for war games or any sort of shooters really, but I got this 90% off and figured it couldn't hurt to try. As someone who hated Atomic Heart, only played a few hours max of Helldivers 2, etc. etc... this game is marvelous. The guns feel great, the characters feel human, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is this game wacky. I didn't expect to care much for the story, but I liked all of the characters somehow! I appreciate that everyone truly spoke with their heart unabashedly, certainly not something you find in most rough-and-tumble shooters. There was emotion without it being too heavy handed, and lore if you chose to listen to the 5 minute monologues; times to rest, times to plan, times to think about your actions. It isn't the most amazing game ever, and has corrupted a save file or two in my time playing, but I always was happy to return or replay a level. It's carved a little space out in my very picky gamer heart and I can't complain. Very fun little game, lots to do and replay!

I would say Metro 2033 Exodus is the most playable game in the Triology. Despite several absurb bugs and awkward cutscenes, I kinda enjoyed the game (MOST importantly, without annoying crash like the two previous games). 
The game is well-written and stick to the original story, which was stunningly visualized with the next-gen graphics and designs. I can see a huge progress in gameplay and above all the attention to details.
Speaking of the negative experiences, I have to admit that 4A team needs to put more effort in making saving mechanism better in the future products. I have to constantly manual save my games to avoid the absurdity that the same cut-scence is replayed many times. 
Nevertheless this is still a good game with solid story-telling, authentic character interaction, stunning environment and indeed novel-based world-building. 
7/10 TBH
